goals.name: SQL parameter arrays and truthful bulk capabilities

goals.name: Native execution identity

goals.acceptance: A new execution omits its ID or resume omits the original ID. Current ABI 10 source and behavioral evidence required.

goals.name: Source record error ports
goals.verification: NotRun
goals.trigger: A recoverable CSV/NDJSON/SQL record contains invalid field content.
goals.baselineFinding: Data cursors return field parse errors and SQL source has no unified per-record error channel.
goals.acceptance: A recoverable CSV/NDJSON/SQL record contains invalid field content. Current ABI 10 source and behavioral evidence required.
goals.progress: CSV/NDJSON isolate bounded record errors through the shared native error schema and existing output ports. Normal/error Snapshot batches retain their output port and physical record identity. SQL source record isolation and commit/recovery closure remain pending.

goals.name: Expression transform row errors
goals.verification: NotRun
goals.trigger: A Derived Column or Conditional Split expression fails for one record.
goals.baselineFinding: Expression row evaluation can fail an activation; recoverable row attribution must share Data error metadata.
goals.acceptance: A Derived Column or Conditional Split expression fails for one record. Current ABI 10 source and behavioral evidence required.
goals.progress: Cast, Derived Column and Conditional Split use one native status classification and error record writer. Execution failures cannot be ignored or redirected. Additional expression failure attribution and complete product acceptance remain pending.

goals.name: Destination isolation and error barrier
goals.verification: NotRun
goals.trigger: Normal and rejected rows share a batch or a SQL statement fails for a record.
goals.baselineFinding: Destination ordinary failures stop flow; both error and regular target confirmation must remain one barrier.
goals.acceptance: Normal and rejected rows share a batch or a SQL statement fails for a record. Current ABI 10 source and behavioral evidence required.
goals.progress: SQL destination shares ud_record_error and an optional error port. Under declared participants, an optimistic batch is isolated with Native savepoints, then failed records use parameter binding. Execution faults cannot redirect; provider codes are sanitized. Real dual-target recovery remains pending.

limitations: No arbitrary global distributed transaction or general exactly-once guarantee
Advanced protocols, CDC/SCD/Fuzzy and BI Planner remain outside the current core acceptance
Single-session container transactions; arbitrary resource combinations and transactional child checkpoints are rejected before effects
Query/Schema enumerators have no reproducible external snapshot token and reject checkpoint resume
Recovery plans serialize tree scheduling; operator partitions merge in deterministic partition order
Source ranges and round-robin partitions are stable logical row positions; file partitions scan the authorized immutable source instead of assuming record-safe byte offsets
Driver/external RSS is outside the native allocator quota; benchmark RSS is measured separately
Advanced SSIS components and BI Planner remain their existing Planned/Partial status; all 69 goals are retained
Pool reuse requires UD_CONNECT_POOL and a successful native reset_session; unknown third-party session state is closed instead of reused
PostgreSQL module requires libpq >=17 for nonblocking cancellation; tested against a disposable local server, without production connections
Float64 SUM preserves serial input order and reports effective partition count 1; integer/Decimal SUM uses exact private 256-bit partial state and checks the public range only at final output
Runtime task/pipeline diagnostic records are bounded at 1024/256 and report dropped counts; callback events remain the complete optional host stream
Windows is exempt by explicit user instruction; no Windows compilation, runtime or binary certification is claimed
Execution caches require one builder and do not publish from an active transaction; cross-execution reuse is not implicit.
Incremental confirmation is a whole-DataFlow receipt barrier; active-transaction incremental sources are explicitly Unsupported.
Canonical SQLite exact NUMERIC/Decimal and PostgreSQL unbounded numeric or timestamp without time zone require a supported declared domain instead of guessed conversions.
Immutable journal Wire payloads remain owned by the state directory through resume; the host retires that directory after retention requirements are met.
ABI 7 row identity/rule metadata increases sort spill traffic. The matching CSV workload regressed against the historical ABI 6 baseline; six workload results do not imply a universal speedup.

Bounded implementation review: preserve ENUM ordinal zero and SET bitmaps with ordered UINT64 dictionaries; string labels cannot distinguish empty/numeric labels and empty sets. Native SQL scans explicitly project unsigned values and controlled LOAD DATA explicitly assigns numeric values; session variables are cleared.

Bounded implementation review: record absence differs from NULL; Changesets preserve it in Native Batch/Wire and only assign present values. Operations unable to represent partial images reject them. Source normal/error batches share Snapshot storage with persisted output port and physical source position.
Acquire and capability-check every participant before effects; durably identify participants before prepare; persist commit/rollback decision before phase-two commands.
Recovery follows the durable decision; no source cursor acknowledgement before ordinary/error destinations, transaction outcome and epoch state are jointly confirmed.
Plain REST unknown submission is RecoveryRequired and cannot be automatically replayed; explicit idempotent/receipt modes declare only proven guarantees.

Compatible schema change drains at the epoch barrier, maps stable field identities, rebinds affected components and persists schema version; incompatible changes preserve position/event without confirming cursor.
File append/overwrite uses controlled generations, original checksum and atomic publish; recovery checks publication facts rather than overwriting old artifacts.
Catalog uses SQLite transactions/WAL/indexes for multi-process management; execution correctness remains in Journal, not service memory or Catalog inference.
Durable queued jobs survive restart; concurrent limits and retry bounds are enforced, and unknown commit disables automatic retry.
Concentrated compile/test gates follow coherent implementation. Windows and Linux are required; missing acceptance resources remain Blocked.

Bounded transaction implementation review: prepared-ID disappearance alone is not a COMMIT proof. Each participant stores its binding digest with business effects; recovery checks prepared listings and visible receipts. Journal task/batch/cursor facts stay under the transaction owner until all participant outcomes resolve; completion logging precedes retiring pending facts. Required policy declares participants and needs an authorized state directory; unsupported resources are rejected before business effects.
